newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK banks seen posting satisfactory growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: HK banks seen posting satisfactory growth in 1997.

text.p: The performance of Hong Kong's banking sector should be satisfactory in 1997, Hongkong Bank executive director Vincent Cheng said on Monday.

"If you look at the banking sector of Hong Kong as a whole, we saw reasonable loan growth and therefore I would expect the banking sector's performance this year should be satisfactory," he told Reuters in an interview.
Hongkong Bank parent HSBC Holdings Plc posted growth of 25 percent in attributable profit in 1996.

Cheng said a combination of that strong growth and confidence in Hong Kong's future after the territory returns to Chinese rule at midnight of June 30 was helping to boost HSBC shares to record levels.

"Our results last year were very good -- as you could see all our subsidiaries are making very strong profit growth ... 1997 risk has been exaggerated and therefore there is a lot of discounting in the share market in Hong Kong," said Cheng.
HSBC shares fell HK$2.00 to HK$233.00 on Monday after setting a record high of HK$235.00 on Friday.
